title: Native Weil underived adjunction and K-injective direct-image model
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$, an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k_0$ and $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a separated finite-type morphism between separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes. Use the actual coefficient sheaves $B_T$, module categories $\mathcal A_T$, Frobenius functors $P_T=F_T^*$ and abelian fixed-pair categories $\mathcal W_T=\mathcal A_T^{F_T^*}$ of [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework], with its small-site and larger-universe convention. For $T=X,Y$, the category $\mathcal A_T$ of $B_T$-module objects in sheaves of $\Omega$-vector spaces is equivalent, preserving kernels, to the category of sheaves of $B_T$-modules. The categories $\mathcal A_T$ and $\mathcal W_T$ are Grothendieck abelian [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], $P_T$ is an additive autoequivalence, and the forgetful functor $U_T:\mathcal W_T\to\mathcal A_T$ is exact and conservative. Every cochain complex in $\mathcal W_T$ admits a quasi-isomorphism to a K-injective complex (every chain map from an acyclic complex is null-homotopic).

Write $L=\bar f^*$ and $R=\bar f_*$ for the actual module inverse and direct images with the framework's coefficient map. Their specified adjunction, with unit $\eta$ and counit $\varepsilon$, lifts through the framework's Frobenius comparisons to an additive adjunction $F_0:\mathcal W_Y\rightleftarrows\mathcal W_X:G_0$ whose carrier unit and counit are $\eta$ and $\varepsilon$. These $F_0,G_0$ are precisely the underived native Weil inverse and direct images. The functor $F_0$ is exact, and termwise $G_0$ carries K-injectives in $\mathcal W_X$ to K-injectives in $\mathcal W_Y$.

Put $Q_T:K(\mathcal W_T)\to D(\mathcal W_T)$ for localization of cochain complexes modulo homotopy. The termwise homotopy adjunction sends $[u:F_0M\to I]$ to $[G_0u\circ\eta_M]$, with inverse $[v:M\to G_0I]\mapsto[\varepsilon_I\circ F_0v]$. The actual ambient pullback is $f^*=D(F_0)$. The actual ambient direct image is the total right derived functor $RG_0=Rf_*$ with universal comparison $\beta:Q_YG_0\Rightarrow Rf_*Q_X$ of [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. Its components $\beta_I$ are invertible at K-injective $I$. For every K-injective resolution $r:J\to I$, the canonical computation isomorphism is
$$c_r=\beta_I^{-1}\circ Rf_*(Q_Xr):Rf_*(Q_XJ)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_YG_0I.$$
For every homotopy-class map $v:I\to I'$ between K-injectives, the computation respects maps by
$$Rf_*(Q_Xv)\circ\beta_I=\beta_{I'}\circ Q_Y(G_0v).$$
All resolutions here are in the abelian Weil categories, without replacing $D(\mathcal W_T)$ by fixed pairs in another derived category. No bounded constructible restriction or derived adjunction is asserted.

proof.text: For $T=X,Y$, put $S=\underline\Omega$ on the stipulated small site. By [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework], $B_T$ is a sheaf of commutative $S$-algebras and the ambient tensor is over $S$. Apply [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] with $\mathcal O=S$: an internal action $B_T\otimes_S M\to M$ is exactly a restriction-compatible $S$-bilinear pairing $(b,m)\mapsto bm$. Its unit and associativity identities are precisely $1m=m$ and $(bb')m=b(b'm)$ on sections. Conversely a sheaf of $B_T$-modules has its $S$-action by restriction along $S\to B_T$, and its sectionwise multiplication gives that tensor action. An internal module morphism is precisely a $B_T$-linear sheaf map. These constructions are mutually inverse on objects and maps; the recovered $S$-action is the original one since $(s1)m=sm$. The kernel consists of the same local sections killed by the map, with the restricted action, so this equivalence preserves kernels.

source.place: Section 03EK (section-tensor-product), paragraph defining sheaf tensor by bilinear maps, following lemma-sheafification-tensor; agent application with base ring sheaf underline Omega

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck] to the small representative site and the actual commutative ring sheaf $B_T$. The size hypothesis holds in the larger coefficient universe stipulated by [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework]. Step 1 transfers its abelian structure, colimits, exact filtered colimits and generator to $\mathcal A_T$: an equivalence carries universal cones and cocones to universal ones, carries kernels and cokernels to kernels and cokernels, and its Hom bijections carry a generator to a generator. Hence $\mathcal A_T$ is Grothendieck abelian. By [lem-sf-native-adic-pullback-frobenius-mates], $P_T$ is an additive autoequivalence. Specialize [lem-sf-fixed-pair-derived-forget-comparison] to $\mathcal C=\mathcal D=\mathcal A_T$, both endofunctors $P_T$, and $L=\mathrm{id}$ with identity exchange. Its first paragraph gives that $\mathcal W_T$ is Grothendieck abelian and $U_T$ is exact and conservative. This uses the abelian fixed-pair category, not a category of fixed pairs formed after localization.

For the given $f_0$, [lem-sf-native-adic-pullback-frobenius-mates] supplies additive $L\dashv R$, exact $L$, and the actual comparisons $e:P_XL\cong LP_Y$, $b:P_YR\cong RP_X$, including the assertion that $b$ is the mate of $e^{-1}$. Thus [lem-sf-fixed-pair-adjunction-lift] applies with $\mathcal C=\mathcal A_Y$, $\mathcal D=\mathcal A_X$, $F=P_Y$, $G=P_X$. Its lifts send $(M,\phi)$ to $(LM,L(\phi)e_M)$ and $(N,\psi)$ to $(RN,R(\psi)b_N)$, exactly the functors in [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework]. It gives $F_0\dashv G_0$ with carrier unit $\eta$ and counit $\varepsilon$. Both lifts are additive because their maps are the additive carrier maps and addition is inherited from carriers. Since $\mathcal A_X,\mathcal A_Y$ are Grothendieck abelian by step 2 and have Hom sets small in the framework's coefficient universe, they have all small limits and colimits by [lem-sfb-grothendieck-filtered-finite-limits], so [lem-sf-fixed-pair-created-abelian-structure] applies to $(\mathcal A_T,P_T)$: forgetting reflects exactness. Since $U_XF_0=LU_Y$ and both $L,U_Y$ are exact, $F_0$ preserves short exact sequences, hence is exact.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-grothendieck-k-injective] to each Grothendieck abelian category $\mathcal W_T$ from step 2. Every complex has a quasi-isomorphism to a K-injective complex inside this very abelian category. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] with $\mathcal A=\mathcal W_X$, $\mathcal B=\mathcal W_Y$, $u=G_0$, $v=F_0$. The additive adjunction and exactness of $v$ were established in step 3. Consequently termwise $G_0$ sends every K-injective Weil complex to a K-injective Weil complex.

The termwise unit and counit of step 3 are chain maps by naturality with each differential. For a chain map $u:F_0M\to I$, set $T(u)=G_0u\circ\eta_M$; for $v:M\to G_0I$, set $S(v)=\varepsilon_I\circ F_0v$. The triangle identities and naturality give $ST(u)=u$ and $TS(v)=v$ degreewise. These formulas descend to chain homotopy: if $u-u'=d_Ih+h d_{F_0M}$, with $h^n:F_0M^n\to I^{n-1}$, then $G_0(h)\eta_M$ is a homotopy from $T(u)$ to $T(u')$, by additivity and naturality of $\eta$; if $v-v'=d_{G_0I}k+k d_M$, then $\varepsilon_I F_0(k)$ is a homotopy from $S(v)$ to $S(v')$. The same degreewise naturality makes $T,S$ natural in chain maps of both variables, hence in their homotopy classes. This proves precisely the stated homotopy adjunction and its two formulas. No injectivity or boundedness is needed for this step.

proof.text: Since $F_0$ is exact, [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] gives its termwise descent $D(F_0)$. It is the actual ambient $f^*$ by [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework]. For additive $G_0$, [lem-trf-additive-homotopy-triangulated] gives the triangulated functor $K(G_0)$; localization $Q_Y$ is triangulated by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] to $Q_YK(G_0)$, using the resolutions of step 4. Its total right derived functor exists and the universal comparison is invertible on K-injectives. By [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] this is $(RG_0,\beta)$; the framework's $Rf_*$ denotes this very total right derivation. Thus $\beta:Q_YG_0\Rightarrow Rf_*Q_X$, with each $\beta_I$ invertible at K-injective $I$.

proof.text: For a resolution $r:J\to I$, localization makes $Q_Xr$ invertible; applying $Rf_*$ and composing with $\beta_I^{-1}$ therefore gives the canonical isomorphism $c_r=\beta_I^{-1}Rf_*(Q_Xr)$. It has source $Rf_*(Q_XJ)$ and target $Q_YG_0I$. Naturality of the comparison transformation at any homotopy-class map $v:I\to I'$ reads $Rf_*(Q_Xv)\circ\beta_I=\beta_{I'}\circ Q_Y(G_0v)$, exactly the asserted equation. These arguments use only the localization and the universal comparison already obtained in step 6 and apply to arbitrary unbounded complexes. All resolutions remain in $\mathcal W_T$.
